about: Settings atlas offers at install and lets you change at any time. Claude Code settings are opt-in, explained, diffed, backed up and reversible; atlas's own switches are on by default and explained at install. Values were measured on real sessions; see 'basis'.

settings.title: Keep subagents' prompt cache for an hour
settings.what: Subagents normally keep their prompt cache for 5 minutes. When one waits longer than that (a build, a test run), its whole context is written to the cache again on the next turn.
settings.cost: Cache writes cost 2x the input price instead of 1.25x, but the full re-writes after idle waits stop.
settings.basis: 69 builder lanes: 130 M of 155 M cache-write tokens were full re-writes after idles (wiki: Token savings and method).

settings.title: Fewer goal check-ins while background work runs
settings.what: With a /goal set, Claude Code wakes the session to check on background work after 30 min, then 1 h, then every 2 h. Each wake re-reads the whole conversation. This makes it 2 h, then 4 h, then every 8 h. Results from finished work still wake the session as before.
settings.cost: You hear about stuck background work later. Setting 0 turns check-ins off but also turns off automatic retries after transient errors, so atlas offers 120 and warns before 0.
settings.basis: Long sessions process 0.7-1.8 G tokens; each wake at 300k context costs about 300k tokens of cache reads.

warn.0: 0 turns check-ins off AND turns off automatic retries after transient errors.

settings.title: Route large tool results through atlas
settings.what: atlas's hooks keep a large shell, build, Read or Grep result on disk and hand the model a short digest plus a handle; it pulls exact slices by handle when it needs them. Small results pass through untouched, and any hook error passes the call through as it was.
settings.cost: A digest can hide a line the model then has to slice for (one more tool call). The full output stays on disk under the handle.
settings.basis: Long-session attribution: shell reads are 36% and build/test output 6% of weighted tokens; those results enter the context whole without routing.

settings.title: Update atlas at session start
settings.what: Before the server starts, atlas checks the latest release (at most once an hour), verifies its signature and swaps it in. Offline, or on any error, the installed version starts.
settings.cost: Up to about 10 s at a session start that finds a new release; past that the current version starts and the update finishes for the next start.
settings.basis: Releases are signed (ed25519, public key built in); a bad or missing signature is refused.
settings.default_note: atlas default: on; set update-pin to stay on one version

settings.title: Stay on one atlas version
settings.what: Pins atlas to the named version: the updater installs it if needed and never moves past it.
settings.cost: No fixes or improvements arrive until the pin is removed.
settings.basis: For a known-good build, or a machine that must not change.

settings.title: Cap how many agents of each kind run at once
settings.what: The PreToolUse hook counts the session's running agents by kind (builders, reviewers, research) and denies a launch past its kind's cap, with a reason telling the session to queue it. It never allows a call, so permission prompts are unchanged. See the orchestrate skill and docs/design/orchestrate.md.
settings.cost: A launch past a cap waits for a running agent to finish. Fan-outs of many small agents need a higher research cap or a Kind line in their briefs.
settings.basis: Long multi-agent sessions on one machine: more than two compiling agents at once kept a compiler running all the time, and measured runs starved waiting for a quiet machine.

settings.title: Experimental, off by default: manage the memory folder and rule files
settings.what: atlas finds the project's Claude Code memory folder and root CLAUDE.md and keeps them in its store. A query that hits a replaced ruling answers with the live one, tagged with what it replaces, and hook pointers on rules and memories are one-line headlines. Never asked: turn it on with atlas settings set memory-rules true. atlas settings off memory-rules removes the key, back to unset. Setting false is not the same as unset: it also stops sync and query recall of the memory and rule files the configuration names by hand, and keeps the store. See https://github.com/bloodfeast/atlas/wiki/Memory-and-rule-files.
settings.cost: Nothing in your files is rewritten. A headline holds less of a ruling, so an agent may need one more recall to read it. On a test set, not a promise: the 1.5x token bar was missed (hook 1.027x, query 0.921x, so a query costs more), memory-eval strict pass fell from 98 to 82 and tokens per question rose 13%.
settings.basis: A 1,582-item rules file: a reversal word finds most reversals, and only about 1 in 12 names the record it reverses, so the rest are asked (atlas rules sitting).
settings.default_note: atlas default: unset, what the configuration names by hand stays as it is

warn.true: experimental: known limits are listed at https://github.com/bloodfeast/atlas/wiki/Memory-and-rule-files.
warn.false: false is not unset: it also stops sync and query recall of the memory and rule files the configuration names by hand. atlas settings off memory-rules returns to unset.

settings.title: Builders at once
settings.what: How many agents that write and compile code may run at once while agent caps are on. Clamped to Claude Code's own limit (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS, 20 by default). 0 launches none.
settings.cost: Higher runs more compiles at once: faster queues, a busier machine.
settings.basis: Two builders left the machine quiet often enough for clean measurements.

settings.title: Reviewers at once
settings.what: How many read-only review agents may run at once while agent caps are on. Clamped to Claude Code's own limit. 0 launches none.
settings.cost: Higher spends more tokens at once on reviews.
settings.basis: The same practice as the builder cap: two reviewers and one research agent beside two builders.

settings.title: Research and design agents at once
settings.what: How many research or design agents may run at once while agent caps are on (Claude Code's Explore and Plan agents count here). Clamped to Claude Code's own limit. 0 launches none.
settings.cost: Higher allows wider fan-outs of searches.
settings.basis: The same practice as the builder cap: two reviewers and one research agent beside two builders.

settings.title: How agents' context limits are applied
settings.what: Past its handoff point an agent is told to wrap up and hand off at its next clean stopping point. Past its hard limit, enforced denies every tool but the handoff (and any resume of the agent); advisory only tells it; off does nothing. Per-kind values in the configuration override this.
settings.cost: Enforced can stop an agent mid-step if it ignores the wrap-up warnings; the handoff tool always still runs.
settings.basis: Agents resumed near a full 1M window re-read their whole context on every turn; fresh agents started from the handoff and the lane journal lost nothing.

settings.title: An agent's hard context limit
settings.what: The context size, in tokens, by which an agent must have handed off, for every kind without its own limit.
settings.cost: Higher lets agents run longer before a fresh one takes over; each turn past it re-reads a larger context.
settings.basis: Handoffs between about 285k and 450k context on a 1M window left room to finish the current step.
settings.default_note: atlas default: 450,000 scaled to the context window

settings.title: Where an agent is told to wrap up
settings.what: The context size, in tokens, from which an agent is told to wrap up and write its handoff at its next clean stopping point, for every kind without its own handoff point. At most the hard limit.
settings.cost: Lower hands off sooner: more fresh agents, each cheaper per turn.
settings.basis: Agents told to wrap up from about 285k on a 1M window handed off with room left to finish their current step.
settings.default_note: atlas default: 285,000 scaled to the context window
